Steps: (1) filter FREQ=="Q" for the quarterly dataset (FREQ Y rows are the annual averages — ship separately or drop). Numbers are already numeric in the CSV — no European-format cleanup needed. Build meta dimension levels from distinct (INDICATORS_HRCHY, DETAILS_DE); EN labels are NOT in the file (only FR/DE) but DETAILS codes are language-neutral NOGA letters — hardcode EN section names (A=Agriculture, B-F=Industry/construction, G-T=Services, plus the 19 section letters) or set label to the NOGA code.

spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse R/source_fso_excel.R::fso_excel_download (order resolution + binary download + pubdate) and add ONE bespoke parser fso_excel_ch_fso_construction_inv(path, pubdate) in R/source_fso_excel_sets.R, anchored on HEADER TEXT (per repo convention). Steps per sheet: (1) skip any sheet whose top ~14 rows contain no "Mio" -> drops the provisional 2024-2025 %-only sheet. (2) year = as.integer(substr(trimws(sheet),1,4)) = the Investitionen year. (3) group cols: find the row (<=8) containing both literal "Tiefbau" and "Hochbau"; tief_col/hoch_col = their column positions. (4) unit row: among rows 1..12 pick the one with the MOST cells matching /Mio/ (>=2) — NOT the first match, because old 2005-2012 sheets carry the title line "In Mio. Fr., zu laufenden Preisen" on row 2 which is a false positive; the real per-column "in Mio. Fr." sub-headers (rows 5 or 9) have 2-4 matches. (5) mio_cols = which cells in unit row match /Mio/; Tiefbau Investitionen value column = min(mio_cols >= tief_col), Hochbau = min(mio_cols >= hoch_col) — picking the FIRST "in Mio. Fr." in each group selects Investitionen and skips the second one (Arbeitsvorrat/backlog). (6) Total data row = first row below unit row where any cell trimws=="Total" (col1 in 13-col sheets, col2 in 26-col 2007-2012 sheets — found by trim match, robust to the spacer-column shift). (7) parse_num: strip apostrophe thousands sep, comma->dot decimal, "..."->NA (same as fso_excel_ch_fso_cpi). (8) total = tiefbau+hochbau (verified internally consistent). Emit long: dim col `werk` in {tiefbau,hochbau,total}, date=YYYY-01-01 ISO, value=CHF mn. Meta dimensions$werk$levels with multilingual labels (de Tiefbau/Hochbau/Total, en Civil engineering/Building construction/Total). Verified vs repo's own known-good extract: 2007=47459.8, 2012=56268.3, 2013=58783.5, 2019=61339.7 all match to the decimal; full 2005-2023 series prototyped at /tmp/ds-spike/parse3.R.

spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse R/source_fso_excel.R::fso_excel_download("je-d-04.02.06.01") to get the master xlsx + pubdate (verified: asset 32627391, embargo 2024-10-28). Two sheets: "BIP pro Kanton" (93 rows) and "BIP pro Grossregion" (36 rows). Each sheet has THREE stacked blocks separated by a blank col1 row: (1) absolute LEVELS "In ... CHF zu laufenden Preisen", (2) YoY %-change current prices, (3) YoY %-change prior-year prices. Keep block 1 ONLY. Mechanical parse (anchored on HEADER TEXT, never index, per repo convention): read with col_names=FALSE; find header row where trimws(col1) == "Kanton" (or "Grossregion"); years live in that header row cols 2..N -> strip non-digits with gsub('[^0-9]','') to turn "2022p" into 2022, keep cols whose value is a 4-digit year; iterate rows from header+1 downward, BREAK on first blank/NA col1 (ends the levels block before the %-change blocks), SKIP the "In ... CHF" subheader row (grepl('^In .*CHF')); for each region row emit region-code + date=as.Date(YYYY-01-01) + value=as.numeric(cell). Tag canton sheet rows level='canton', region sheet rows level='greater_region'. Combine. Verified prototype in /tmp/ds-spike/parse.R produced 525 rows; both the 26-canton sum and the 7-region sum equal the Switzerland total 791087.2 mn for 2022 (exact), confirming correct slicing. Dimension codes: prefer BFS canton numbers / 2-letter abbrev (ZH,BE,...) by row position; greater regions get slugs (lake_geneva, espace_mittelland, nordwest, zurich, ostschweiz, zentralschweiz, ticino, CH). Multilingual labels: download the EN master (je-e-04.02.06.01, asset 32627406) once and map labels by identical row position (verified: same order, e.g. Zurich/Geneva/Ticino/Switzerland); FR/IT masters exist too (je-f-/je-i-) for full multilingual meta. New bespoke parser belongs in R/source_fso_excel_sets.R as fso_excel_gdp_region() returning list(id,data,meta).
spikes.effort: moderate: the fetch/resolve is trivial (existing DAM helper, single asset, two clean tabular sheets). The only real work is one bespoke per-sheet parser (3 stacked blocks -> keep block 1, break on blank row, skip units subheader) plus building the canton/region code+multilingual-label map from the EN/FR/IT master files. ~1 helper function modeled on existing fso_excel_* parsers.
spikes.gotchas: (1) LEVELS ONLY in the first block — the 2nd/3rd blocks are %-change (current-price and prior-year-price/real growth) and must be dropped; the break-on-blank-row logic handles this, but a naive read_excel of the whole sheet would mix them. (2) Values are CURRENT-PRICE (nominal) levels only ("zu laufenden Preisen"); there is NO real/chained absolute level series in this file (real growth appears only as the %-change block). So this complements ch_seco_gdp (which has real/quarterly national GDP) as a nominal regional cut, not a real one. (3) Latest year is provisional ("2022p"); the series lags ~2 years (annual regional accounts are inherently late) — coverage ends 2022 as of the 2024-10-28 edition. (4) Both levels (canton + greater region) repeat "Zurich" and "Switzerland"; the level dimension disambiguates — do not dedupe across levels, and do not sum across the two levels. (5) License: FSO terms (use existing license='fso'); open and free. (6) opendata.swiss CKAN must be hit at ckan.opendata.swiss with a browser User-Agent (the bare opendata.swiss/api host 302-redirects). (7) Not on SDMX — do not re-search disseminate.stats.swiss for this; DAM Excel is the channel.

spikes.parse_recipe: New tiny module on the DAM-CSV channel (this is a single tidy long CSV, NOT the multi-sheet construction-investment Excel, so do NOT reuse the source_fso_excel per-sheet stitch). Steps: (1) curl/get the master CSV (UTF-8 BOM; read with col_types=cols(.default=col_character())). (2) filter UNIT_MEAS=="MCHF" to keep current-price levels (drop AC and ACPP which are %-change). (3) transmute sector=SECTOR, asset=CLASSIFICATION, date=as.Date(to_iso(PERIOD)) [reuse R/dates.R::to_iso; PERIOD is YYYY -> first-of-year], value=as.numeric(VALUE); drop NA values; arrange(sector,asset,date). (4) frequency via infer_frequency() -> "annual". (5) Build dimensions meta from the appendix ODS codelist sheets (SECTOR, CLASSIFICATION) which are already en/de/fr/it -> mirror the multilingual levels shape that .seco_dimensions builds; set asset hierarchy P51G -> {construction (P5111_N111_112G) -> {6011 Hochbau, 6010 Tiefbau}, equipment (P5111_N113T117G)} and sector hierarchy S1 -> {S11,S12(->S121T127,S12Q),S13(->S1314),S14,S15}. license="fso". Verified end-to-end with /tmp/ds-spike/proto.R sourcing R/dates.R: 1086 rows, annual, 1995-2024, internal consistency holds (construction+equipment=224331.05=P51G total; Hochbau 54715.2 + Tiefbau 11919.6 = construction 66634.8).
spikes.effort: moderate: the fetch+parse is trivial (clean long CSV, reuse to_iso/infer_frequency), but writing the multilingual dimension+hierarchy meta from the appendix codelist sheets and choosing the asset/sector split dimension for the Display hint is the only real work. ~1 small new helper, no new dependency (ODS read via unzip+content.xml or hardcode the small fixed codelist).
spikes.gotchas: (1) Confirms the deferred-datasets steer: GFCF detail is NOT on FSO SDMX (enumerated all 182 dataflows - no national-accounts/GFCF/P51 flow) and STAT-TAB is dead from this env; the live channel is opendata.swiss CKAN -> DAM CSV. (2) opendata.swiss redirects to ckan.opendata.swiss and needs a browser User-Agent (use the source_ffa.R UA pattern). (3) File mixes three UNIT_MEAS in one column - MUST filter to MCHF or you triple-count and mix levels with percentages (this is the trap the construction-investment dataset fell into; here the levels DO exist for the full 1995-2024 span, unlike construction which lost levels after 2019). (4) asset code "Fixed assets and software" (P5111_N113T117G) is labelled "Ausruestungen/equipment" in DE and is really equipment+IP/software, not just machinery; keep the FSO English label. (5) P51G total is published only for S1 (total economy); sub-sectors give construction+equipment that sum to their implicit total - 37 series not 45. (6) This is strictly MORE detailed than ch_seco_gdp, which already carries coarse inv_gfcf/inv_constr/inv_fixed (P51G/P5111_N111_112G/P5111_N113T117G) for the total economy only and NO institutional-sector or Hochbau/Tiefbau split - so the gap (by-sector + civil/building engineering split) is real and non-overlapping. (7) License = opendata.swiss terms_by (free reuse, attribution) = the repo's existing license:"fso". spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse R/source_fso_excel.R::fso_asset_master("ts-x-04.07.01.01") to resolve the asset, then grab the MASTER link (it is a CSV, not xlsx, for this asset) and download_binary() it. NOTE: this asset's master is .csv — either pass a .csv tempfile to download_binary or fetch the master URL directly. Parse is trivial (no bespoke sheet parser needed): read.csv(file, fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM"). Columns: PERIOD (year int), INDICATOR (one of "GDP","Actual hours worked","Productivity"), UNIT_MEA (constant "Index"), VALUE (numeric), OBS_STATUS (constant "R" = revised). Map INDICATOR to slugs gdp/hours/productivity, build date=as.Date(paste0(PERIOD,"-01-01")), value=as.numeric(VALUE). Drop UNIT_MEA (single value) and OBS_STATUS. Output tidy long: indicator, date, value (102 rows). pubdate from fso_asset_master()$pubdate -> meta$updated.
spikes.effort: trivial — already tidy long CSV behind the existing DAM helper; no SDMX, no multi-sheet xlsx stitch, no cell caps. One new wrapper function alongside fso_sdmx/excel sets, ~15 lines. Build a datasheet datasets/ch_fso_labour_productivity.md.
spikes.gotchas: 1) The legacy "duplicate idx (gdp/ahw/prd)" error: all three indicators share UNIT_MEA="Index", so any pivot keyed on UNIT collides. Key the dimension on INDICATOR, not on UNIT_MEA — this is why the clean structure works. 2) This master link is a CSV (most DAM masters are xlsx); set the tempfile extension to .csv when reusing fso_excel_download, or download the master URL directly. 3) UTF-8 BOM on the CSV — use fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM" (or strip BOM) so the first header isn't read as "i..PERIOD". 4) It is an INDEX (base 1991=100), NOT a level (CHF/hour) and NOT a %-change — frame the Display as level=index. Sibling datasets exist at current prices (je-d-04.07.04.04) and by branch/region if a levels/sector breakdown is later wanted, but the headline GDP-per-hour index is this one. 5) License = fso (BFS open terms, free, source attribution). Display defaults: split=indicator (multi-line: GDP, Actual hours worked, Productivity all comparable on 1991=100), default indicator=productivity, transform=index, frequency=annual, topic="National economy"/"National accounts".
spikes.notes: Headline series matches FSO web page title exactly: "Labour productivity by actual hours worked at previous year's prices - 1991-2024" (https://www.bfs.admin.ch/asset/en/ts-x-04.07.01.01). NOT on SDMX (disseminate.stats.swiss) — enumerated all 182 dataflows for productiv/produktiv/gdp/hour/arbeit, the productivity series is absent; DAM/CKAN is the channel. The three-indicator decomposition (output GDP vs input hours vs resulting productivity) is a nice self-explanatory chart. Multifactor productivity and capital productivity exist as separate CKAN datasets if the concept is later expanded. Recommend ingesting as canonical for "Labour productivity".

spikes.coverage: Semi-annual (Oktober + April reference months), Oct 1998 .. Oct 2025 = 55 periods per series. Workbook = 8 regions (Schweiz + 7 major regions) x 16 work-types x 4 base years (sheets 1998/2010/2015/2020). Proposed catalog slice: Switzerland (REG_01), 3 headline work-types (Total / Hochbau / Tiefbau), base sheet "2020" (Oct 2020=100) = 3 series, 165 long rows. Could optionally expand to all 16 work-types or all 8 regions.
spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse R/source_fso_excel.R::fso_excel_download("cc-t-05.05.01") to get the .xlsx + pubdate. Write a bespoke parser in source_fso_excel_sets.R (one function, like the existing CPI/wages parsers; anchor on HEADER TEXT/TAGS, not column index): (1) read sheet "2020" with col_names=FALSE (base Oct2020=100, newest base, full 1998-2025 history). (2) Header rows: row 5 = reference month word (contains "Okt"->10 else "Apr"->04), row 6 = 4-digit year; val_cols = which(row6 matches ^[0-9]{4}$); build date = as.Date(sprintf("%s-%s-01", year, month)). (3) Column A carries stable tags <REG_nn> (region) and <OBJ_nn> (work-type); column B is the German label. The national block = rows strictly between tag "<REG_01>" (Schweiz) and the next "<REG_" row. (4) Within that block pick work-types by TAG (NOT label text -- the "Baugewerbe : Total" label contains a non-breaking space c2a0 before the colon): <OBJ_02>=Total, <OBJ_03>=Hochbau, <OBJ_13>=Tiefbau. (5) For each, as.numeric the val_cols cells (the literal "..." for missing -> NA, drop), emit long rows work/date/value. Do NOT call to_iso (dates are built directly); HARDCODE meta$frequency="semi-annual" (infer_frequency has no semiannual bucket and would mislabel ~180-day gaps as "annual"). Verified working scratch: /tmp/ds-spike/parse.R against /tmp/ds-spike/copri_u1.xlsx.
spikes.effort: moderate -- one new bespoke per-sheet parser (~30 lines) in source_fso_excel_sets.R + wire into pipeline.R + datasheet. Download/resolve plumbing already exists (fso_excel_download). No new HTTP code. Harder than an SDMX add only because the sheet is row-and-column shaped, but the layout is regular and tag-anchored so no fragile index hunting.
spikes.gotchas: 1) Label encoding trap: "Baugewerbe : Total" has a non-breaking space (0xC2A0) before the colon -- match on the <OBJ_nn> tag in column A, never on label text. 2) Missing cells are the literal "..."/"…" string -> coerce to NA and drop (early periods for newer work-types like Renovation/Einfamilienhaus start ~2010). 3) Multibase workbook: 4 sheets (base 1998/2010/2015/2020 = Oktober each). Pick sheet "2020" for the current canonical base; the legacy dataseries id ch.fso.copri.idx2010 used the 2010 base -- a base re-reference is a level rescale, not a methodology break, but note it (don't splice sheets). 4) This is the construction OUTPUT PRICE index (Baupreisindex) -- distinct from PPI (producer/import prices) and from construction INVESTMENT (Bauinvestitionen, the deferred je-d-09.04.01.27 that is %-change-only after 2019). This one is FULL ABSOLUTE LEVELS through Oct 2025 -- no %-change-only problem. 5) Frequency is semi-annual (only Oct + Apr); represent as first-of-month (10-01 / 04-01). 6) Order cc-d-05.05.01 resolves to a STALE 2021 per-region asset -- use cc-t-05.05.01 for the current multibase national+regional file. 7) License = FSO (free reuse, attribution required), use license:"fso" like sibling FSO datasets.
spikes.notes: Cross-checked against the FSO Oct-2025 press release (asset/en/36262132): headline 116.2 points base Oct2020=100, +0.3% half-year (Apr->Oct), +0.9% YoY. My parse: Total Oct2025=116.2 (exact), Apr2025=115.8 -> +0.35%~=0.3%, Oct2024=115.2 -> +0.87%~=0.9%. Base-period sanity: Total Oct2020=100.0 exactly. Display defaults: split=work (Total/Hochbau/Tiefbau nested under Total), default work=Total, transform=level (index points), seasonal adjustment n/a. Optional richer cut: keep all 16 work-types and/or add region dimension (REG_02..REG_08: Geneva-lake, Espace Mittelland, Northwest, Zurich, East, Central, Ticino) -- the same parser loops naturally over REG blocks. Recommend shipping national headline (3 series) first; this also UN-DEFERS a Prices-domain gap and is cleaner than the deferred Bauinvestitionen.

spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse R/source_fso_sdmx.R::fso_sdmx_fetch UNCHANGED — identical DSD to ch_fso_production. In R/pipeline.R add a tertiary NOGA slice constant (.SDMX_SERVICES_NOGA <- c("G-NxK","G","H","I","J","L","M","N")) and wire: fso_sdmx_fetch("ch_fso_services","CH1.KEU","DF_KEU_Q1","1.0.0", title=list(en="Services-sector turnover (quarterly)"), noga_keep=.SDMX_SERVICES_NOGA). Then add ch_fso_services = list(UNIT_MEASURE = c("VARQ-4","VARQ-1")) to REDUNDANT_LEVELS so the app reproduces YoY/QoQ on the fly from the index (mirrors ch_fso_production exactly). The helper maps TIME_PERIOD (YYYY-Qn) to ISO first-of-period via R/dates.R::to_iso, drops FREQ, reads the four codelists (CL_NOGA_KE etc.) for English labels, and emits the tidy long contract (NOGA,ADJUSTMENT,INDICATOR_KE,UNIT_MEASURE,date,value) + dimensions meta. Verified: 2574 rows, 132 series, dates correct.
spikes.effort: trivial — zero new code; the SDMX helper, date parser, label-from-codelist logic, and REDUNDANT_LEVELS machinery all already exist and are proven on the identical DF_KEU_Q1 flow. Work is one NOGA constant + one fso_sdmx_fetch line in pipeline.R + one REDUNDANT_LEVELS entry + a datasheet (clone ch_fso_production.md). Display defaults: split=NOGA (multi-line breakdown over tertiary subsectors), single-select=ADJUSTMENT,INDICATOR_KE; default NOGA=G-NxK, INDICATOR_KE=UTOT, ADJUSTMENT=Y (seasonally+calendar-adjusted), transform=index. Same pattern as production.
spikes.gotchas: 1) SHORT HISTORY: tertiary codes start 2021-Q1 (only 21 quarters) — services turnover is a newer FSO release, not a fetch limitation; secondary-sector codes in the same flow go to 1999 but tertiary genuinely doesn't. Base year 2021=100. 2) The aggregate label for G-NxK comes back in GERMAN from the codelist name field ('Tertiärer Sektor (ohne...)') because that code's en name is missing — add a tiny label override in the datasheet/wrapper to 'Tertiary sector (excl. financial & insurance)'. Other codes (G,H,I,J,L,M,N) have clean English labels. 3) Levels are INDEX (2021=100), nominal turnover — NO absolute CHF turnover values published, only indices; that is the FSO product, not a parsing loss. 4) UNIT_MEASURE carries redundant VARQ-4/VARQ-1 change leaves that must be pruned via REDUNDANT_LEVELS (the app recomputes them) exactly like ch_fso_production. 5) FSO open-data license ('fso'), free and machine-readable. 6) read_csv emits a harmless duplicate-DATAFLOW-column rename warning (already tolerated for production/retail).
spikes.notes: Complements the existing real-economy turnover set: ch_fso_retail (DF_KEU_M1, NOGA 47) + ch_fso_production (DF_KEU_Q1, secondary B-E/F) + this ch_fso_services (DF_KEU_Q1, tertiary G-NxK..N) cover all three sectors from one well-understood SDMX agency. Live fetch + parse verified end-to-end via /tmp/ds-spike/proto.R using the repo's own helpers (sourced R/http.R, R/dates.R, R/source_fso_sdmx.R). Optionally also offer the monthly flow DF_KEU_M1 for tertiary if FSO publishes monthly tertiary codes there (not checked — quarterly is the canonical services frequency).

spikes.parse_recipe: Reuse fso_excel_download("ts-x-03.02.03.01.02.01") from R/source_fso_excel.R to resolve order nr -> master CSV and download. Then parse exactly like the SDMX-CSV path in R/source_fso_sdmx.R: readr::read_csv(col_types=cols(.default=col_character())); filter to national total (NOGA1=='_T' & SECTOR=='_T' & EMP_STATUS=='_T' & REGION=='_T'); transmute sex=SEX, nat=NAT, worktime=WORKTIME, date=as.Date(to_iso(TIME_PERIOD)) (R/dates.R already maps annual 'YYYY'->'YYYY-01-01'), value=as.numeric(VALUE_W); drop NA; arrange(sex,nat,worktime,date). frequency via infer_frequency(TIME_PERIOD) -> 'annual'. Hand-build dimension label maps (codelists are NOT in this CSV channel): sex{_T=Total,M=Men,F=Women}, nat{_T=Total,SW=Swiss,FOR=Foreign}, worktime{_T=Total,FT=Full-time,PT=Part-time,PT_I=Part-time I (50-89%),PT_II=Part-time II (<50%)}; mark _T as hierarchy parent like fso_sdmx_new_vehicles does. spikes.effort: moderate: download+parse is trivial (clean SDMX-style CSV, helpers already exist), but needs a hand-coded label map (codelists not shipped in this DAM CSV channel) and a choice of which measure(s) to publish. ~1 small parser fn mirroring an existing one.
spikes.gotchas: (1) This is the AVOL 'actual hours worked' cube, NOT a participation/activity rate. The headline Erwerbsquote (economic activity rate, je-d-03.02.01.07.01.01 DAM Excel) is structured as single-year-of-age rows x multi-year PERIOD-BAND columns (1991-1995,...,2021-2023) -> NOT a clean annual time series, so I deliberately picked hours-worked instead; participation-RATE-as-time-series is a separate, messier task. (2) Part-time as a distinct concept is in SDMX (CH1.SAKE/DF_SAKE_TEILZEITGRUND, annual 2010-2025, fetch verified) if a part-time-reasons dataset is wanted later. (3) No codelists in this CSV asset -> dimension labels must be hand-maintained. (4) Asset id 36577051 is mutable on revision; address by order number ts-x-03.02.03.01.02.01, not the bare id. (5) Values are levels (hours), transform=level. (6) License: FSO open (free reuse, attribution) -> license:'fso' like ch_fso_unemp_rate. (7) Series breakdowns are marginals on a national-total cube; FT subdivides into PT only via the WORKTIME total, while PT_I+PT_II are children of PT -> set hierarchy carefully.
spikes.notes: Display defaults: split=worktime (FT vs PT vs total as lines is the story), single-select=sex then nat, default sex=_T/nat=_T/worktime=_T (the 30.9h/week headline FSO quotes), transform=level, seasonal=n/a, units 'Hours per week'. topic='Work and income'. All sample values cross-checked against FSO's own 2024 working-volume press numbers (8.117bn hrs, 30h56min weekly, ~40h full-time).

spikes.parse_recipe: New helper modeled on R/source_fso_sdmx.R's .sdmx_get pattern but pointed at Eurostat. Steps: (1) GET SDMX-CSV from prc_hicp_midx for M.I15.{CP00+CP01..CP12}.CH (request multiple COICOP via + in the key, one call). (2) readr::read_csv all-character (wrap literal body in I() to silence the readr 2.2 warning). (3) transmute item=coicop, date=as.Date(to_iso(TIME_PERIOD)) — REUSE R/dates.R::to_iso (handles YYYY-MM -> ISO first-of-month, already verified), value=as.numeric(OBS_VALUE), filter !is.na(value), arrange(item,date). (4) frequency via R/dates.R::infer_frequency (returns 'monthly', verified). (5) meta$dimensions$item$levels: pull COICOP codelist TSV once, map CP00->'All-items HICP', CP01..CP12 -> division labels (already extracted). Build levels list in the .sdmx_dimensions shape. (6) units = list(en='Index, 2015=100'). Use R/http.R retry wrapper (.with_retry / build httr2 request with req_timeout). Mirror the wrapper shape of fso_sdmx_new_vehicles (returns list(id, data, meta)).
spikes.effort: moderate — the fetch/parse itself is trivial (verified working in /tmp/ds-spike/prototype.R), but it introduces the FIRST Eurostat SDMX endpoint in the repo (existing source_fso_sdmx.R is hardcoded to disseminate.stats.swiss/CH1.KEU codelists), so it needs a small standalone fetcher rather than reusing fso_sdmx_fetch. ~40 lines.
spikes.gotchas: (1) NOT a Swiss-domain source — id prefix ch_fso_ is by convention/concept but data is fetched from Eurostat (ESTAT); document provenance honestly (FSO compiles, Eurostat disseminates). (2) Distinct from ch_fso_cpi/ch_snb_plkopr: HICP excludes owner-occupied housing & health insurance premiums, EU methodology — note in 'What is special'. (3) Unit choice: I15 (2015=100) is current standard and live to 2025-12; a 2025=100 / ECOICOP-v2 re-reference is rolling in at Eurostat — pin unit=I15 explicitly and watch for it being superseded. (4) Levels only available from Dec 2004 (history shorter than LIK's 1982); for long inflation history keep ch_snb_plkopr. (5) Eurostat data may carry OBS_FLAG/CONF_STATUS columns — ignore. (6) License: Eurostat data is free reuse with attribution (cite both FSO as compiler and Eurostat as source). Display defaults: split=item, default item=CP00, transform=yoy, seasonal adjustment=n/a (HICP not seasonally adjusted).
spikes.notes: Live fetch proven via curl and Rscript (/tmp/ds-spike/prototype.R ran clean: 13 series, monthly, 2004-12..2025-12). spikes.parse_recipe: 1) Download the long CSV with the repo helper get_csv / readr::read_csv (URL above). Columns arrive already tidy: structure,type,seas_adj,date,value. 2) filter(!is.na(value)) to drop the 3 ISO-week-53 phantom rows (Dec-28 in 2009/2015/2020). 3) mutate(date=as.Date(to_iso(as.character(date))) [no-op, dates already ISO], value=as.numeric(value)). 4) Drop the two constant columns type (always "index") and seas_adj (always "csa") per source-quirks "drop single-value dimension columns" — keep only structure,date,value. 5) arrange(structure,date). 6) frequency = infer_frequency(raw$date) -> "weekly" (already supported by R/dates.R, returns weekly for ~7-day median gap — no code change needed). 7) Build meta BY HAND (no JSON sidecar exists): one dimension `structure` with two levels seco_wwa and seco_wwa_pre_covid; harvest the multilingual (de/fr/it/en) labels from the xlsx `beschriftung` sheet (verified text e.g. en "Index of weekly economic activity (WEA)" / "Weekly economic activity compared with the pre-crisis level"; units: WEA = scaled to YoY growth rates of real, seasonally/calendar/sport-event-adjusted GDP; pre_covid = % difference to Q4 2019 level). Reuse pattern: closest existing helper is R/source_seco.R::seco_fetch (same DAM + swissdata long CSV shape) but write a sibling seco_wwa_fetch() that hand-builds meta$dimensions instead of remapping a sidecar; reuse R/http.R + R/dates.R::to_iso/infer_frequency + R/io.R writers unchanged.
spikes.effort: moderate (lighter than ch_seco_gdp). Data fetch + parse is trivial (clean long CSV, helpers already handle weekly). The only real work is hand-building the multilingual meta from the xlsx beschriftung sheet because the JSON sidecar that makes ch_seco_gdp a pure passthrough does NOT exist for WWA — so it needs a small bespoke seco_wwa_fetch() rather than reusing seco_fetch verbatim. ~1 short function + 1 datasheet.
spikes.gotchas: 1) NO JSON meta sidecar (the ch_seco_gdp pattern); _json.txt / .json URLs 404 — do not reuse seco_fetch as-is. 2) The values are NOT index levels — they are scaled YoY GDP growth rates (% points): seco_wwa is the weekly proxy for real GDP YoY growth, and seco_wwa_pre_covid is % difference vs the Q4-2019 level. Display transform must be `level` (the value IS already a rate; do NOT apply yoy). 3) Experimental statistic, subject to revision; full 2005+ rescaling happened 2025-10-01 (a methodology break — flag in caveats). 4) seco_wwa_pre_covid is a COVID-era legacy series that stops 2022-12-05 (discontinued); keep it as a non-default alternate, default to seco_wwa. 5) 3 NA rows on Dec-28 of 53-week years — must filter or the writer chokes. 6) type/seas_adj are constant — drop them. 7) Weekly dates are Mondays; do not collapse to monthly. 8) License: SECO terms = free reuse, attribution required (use existing repo license code `seco`); raw data not copyright-protected under Swiss OGD. Suggested Display: split=structure (multi-select), default structure=seco_wwa, transform=level, no seas_adj toggle (single value).

Recommended set: `ogd_ch.kof.esi` (KOF Economic Sentiment Index). Discovery index: GET .../api/v1/public/collections (60 collections; filter is_public=true). Multilingual-ish labels: GET .../api/v1/public/metadata?keys=... (English only). Sibling public sets: `ogd_ch.kof.globalbaro`, `ogd_ch.kof.bts_total`/`bs_indicator`, `ogd_ch.kof.barometer`, `stringency_web`, `ch.kof.jobtracker`, tourism/consensus forecasts.

spikes.parse_recipe: Generalize the existing single-series helper into a public-set helper. In R/source_kof.R add `kof_set_fetch(set, dim_name)`: (1) url <- sprintf(".../api/v1/public/sets/%s?mime=csv", set); (2) raw <- readr::read_csv(get_text(url)) — first col is `date`, remaining cols are the KOF series keys (wide layout); (3) capture raw_periods <- as.character(raw$date) for infer_frequency BEFORE reshaping; (4) date <- as.Date(to_iso(as.character(date))) (monthly "2007-04" -> "2007-04-01", to_iso already handles it); (5) tidyr::pivot_longer(cols=-date, names_to=dim_name, values_to="value"); (6) filter(!is.na(value)) — the wide set is sparse where series start at different dates; (7) value <- as.numeric(value); arrange(dim, date). Verified verbatim in /tmp/ds-spike/prototype.R against /workspace/ds/dataseries-data/R/{http.R,dates.R} (get_text + to_iso + infer_frequency reused unchanged; infer_frequency correctly returns "monthly"). Build meta exactly like kof_fetch: license="kof", source$name=KOF Swiss Economic Institute, source$url from the metadata endpoint (ESI: kof.ethz.ch/en/forecasts-and-indicators/indicators/kof-economic-sentiment-indicator.html). dimensions: one dim named e.g. "indicator" mapping the two raw keys to hardcoded multilingual labels (en/de/fr) in the datasheet — the metadata API only returns English ("KOF Economic Sentiment Indicator for Switzerland, Pre-Brexit version" / "...for Switzerland"), so author de/fr by hand like other datasheets.
spikes.recommended_id: ch_kof_esi (sentiment index). Optional siblings: ch_kof_globalbaro, ch_kof_business_situation. Concept frontmatter: "Business cycle & sentiment / Sentiment composite". Display default: line chart, level (index, mean ~100, unitless), single dim "indicator" with 2 series both visible; reference line at 100.
spikes.effort: trivial — pure additive: one new ~25-line helper kof_set_fetch in the existing R/source_kof.R reusing get_text/to_iso/infer_frequency, plus one datasheet. No new deps (dplyr/tidyr/readr already used). The wide->long pivot is the only new line vs the existing kof_fetch.
spikes.gotchas: 1) THE WEEKLY WBI IS GENUINELY UNAVAILABLE: every WBI-named ts key (ch.kof.wbi/wei/weekly/...) returns HTTP 412, and every WBI-named set 404s. KOF discontinued the COVID-era weekly indicator; it is not in any public set. Do not re-hunt it. 2) The existing ch_kof_barometer datasheet's claim "barometer is the only open KOF key; every other returns 412" is OUTDATED/WRONG at the channel level: it only tested /public/ts?keys=. The open channel is /public/sets/{name} — 30+ sets have is_public=true (verified via /public/collections). Individual ts keys are still gated (412), but the curated OGD sets are open. Worth a one-line correction to that datasheet/source-quirks.md. 3) Sets are WIDE and SPARSE (series have different start dates) — must filter NA after pivot_longer or you get spurious rows. 4) ESI has TWO methodology versions in one set (Pre-Brexit ch.kof.esi.index vs standard .v2018) — keep both as series, label the difference; not a level-vs-change issue (both are index levels). 5) Index is unitless (mean ~100), not a % or growth rate. 6) ESI/barometer are periodically re-based/re-estimated, so the whole back-series can revise (same caveat as the barometer). 7) License = CC BY (opendata.swiss terms_by / opendefinition cc-by, confirmed via ckan.opendata.swiss package_show resource rights) = the existing `kof` license id; redistribution OK with attribution. 8) bts_total/bs_indicator sector balances run back to 1973 quarterly but are diffusion balances (-100..+100), a different scale from the index composites — ship as a separate dataset, not mixed with ESI.
spikes.notes: Recommendation: ship ch_kof_esi as the primary add (cleanest single sentiment composite, monthly, current through 2026-05, direct sibling to the barometer we already have). Optionally also ch_kof_globalbaro (monthly back to 1991) — both are 2-series, trivial. The bigger structural win is generalizing source_kof.R to the sets endpoint, which unlocks a whole family of open KOF data the catalog currently thinks is gated (tourism forecasts, consensus forecast, stringency index, jobtracker, business-situation by sector). Repo helpers reused unchanged: /workspace/ds/dataseries-data/R/http.R (get_text), /workspace/ds/dataseries-data/R/dates.R (to_iso, infer_frequency).

triage.summary: 15 candidates, all verified open (access_verified=true, feasible=yes-easy) - none are infeasible, so the only real decision is sequencing by macro-importance x effort. Six are integrate-now (pure reuse of an existing helper, no new source script): ch_fso_services and ch_fso_cross_border_commuters and ch_fso_pop_detail (FSO SDMX, copy-paste of production/new_vehicles wrappers), ch_fso_labour_productivity (tidy DAM CSV behind fso_asset_master), ch_kof_esi (small sets-endpoint generalization of source_kof.R), and ch_fso_besta_outlook (clone of ch_fso_besta on the working PX-Web besta family). Eight are integrate-with-effort, each needing one bespoke parser, a hand-built label/meta map, license care, or a new endpoint family: ch_fso_trade_partner, ch_fso_ets, ch_fso_gdp_region, ch_fso_construction_prices, ch_fso_gfcf_detail, ch_fso_hicp (first Eurostat endpoint), ch_fso_hours_worked, and ch_seco_wwa (first weekly series). One is defer: ch_fso_construction_inv - feasible and its stale-deferral note is corrected, but it is the most fragile parser and is largely superseded by ch_fso_gfcf_detail's by-sector Hochbau/Tiefbau levels. Key overlaps to respect: GFCF-detail only partially overlaps ch_seco_gdp (new value = institutional-sector + civil/building split; must filter UNIT_MEAS==MCHF); HICP is methodologically distinct from the shipped LIK CPI (excludes owner-occupied housing + health premiums) and is fetched from Eurostat not FSO; trade-by-partner complements (does not duplicate) ch_snb_ausshawarm trade-by-goods; pop_detail is distinct from ch_fso_pop's 1861- balance. Recommended landing order: the six integrate-now first (highest value/lowest cost), then trade_partner + ets + cross-border (flagship labour/external series) and gdp_region, then construction_prices + hicp + hours_worked + wwa, with construction_inv last or dropped.
triage.completeness_verdict: If all 14 feasible adds land, dataseries.org becomes a genuinely strong near-complete open Swiss MACRO catalog - arguably best-in-class for a free aggregator. The core macro skeleton would be covered end to end: national accounts (national GDP + regional GDP + GFCF-by-sector + labour productivity), prices (LIK CPI + HICP + PPI + construction price index), labour (unemployment + BESTA jobs + employment-outlook + ETS headcount + hours worked + cross-border commuters + vacancies + wages), external sector (trade by goods + by partner country + SNB BoP), business cycle/sentiment (KOF barometer + ESI + SECO consumer confidence + the weekly WEA tracker), money/banking/FX (the large SNB block), and demographics (population balance + detailed population). The frequency range would span weekly (WEA) through monthly, quarterly and annual. What stays PERMANENTLY or practically OUT, and why: (1) Sub-annual/sub-national granularity gated behind PX-Web/STAT-TAB/PC-Axis, which is dead from this build environment - canton-level and fine cross-tab cubes beyond what SDMX/DAM expose; this is an infrastructure limit, not a licensing one. (2) BEVNAT vital flows (births/deaths/marriages) as a clean modern time series - only marriages exist on SDMX (2020-2024, too short) and births/deaths live only on dead PX-Web; the long 1861- series is already inside ch_fso_pop, so it is redundant rather than missing. (3) The discontinued KOF weekly WBI - genuinely retired by KOF, not gated. (4) BAZG monthly trade-by-tariff-x-country (since 1988) - the richer upgrade path 502s from this env. (5) Microdata and anything behind authentication or per-key gating (e.g. individual KOF ts keys at HTTP 412), plus commercially-licensed series. (6) True real-time/nowcast and non-official-statistics indicators. (7) Methodology breaks (trade 2013, construction 2012/2013, KOF/WEA rebasings) mean some long series are flagged-but-not-chained, so 'complete continuous history' is partial by design. Net: the catalog would be ~complete for headline open Swiss macro at national level and standard frequencies, but NOT a substitute for FSO's full PX-Web cube universe (fine regional/demographic cross-tabs) nor for microdata - those stay out on infrastructure and scope grounds, not because they are closed.
